newsitem.title: DUBAI: Arab airlines to work to cut European costs.
newsitem.headline: Arab airlines to work to cut European costs.

text.p: Airlines belonging to the Arab Air Carrier Organisation (AACO) have agreed to work together to cut their costs at European airports, the Saudi-based Arab News daily reported on Thursday.

"We have made decisions on the importance of our alliances among us as Arab carriers, and decided to find ways and means of reducing our costs of handling passengers at our European stations," AACO President Hany Aref was quoted as saying.
Aref was speaking after a two-day meeting in Jeddah of the commercial committee of AACO -- which groups 18 Arab carriers.

"One of the most important factors...will be the joint cooperation of all members to work collectively in order to form a block against European airlines. Collective negotiations will be a very effective way to face competition," he said.
Aref said London would be the first station where Arab carriers would work together to reduce costs.

"We will appoint one handling agent for all AACO members flying there by negotiating collectively with handling agents in London. This will reduce costs and will improve the quality of services," he said.
